title: SQL Essentials
description: Covers filtering and sorting rows, joins, grouping and aggregates, NULL handling, subqueries, window ranking, and basic indexing.

questions.prompt: Which clause filters individual rows before any grouping or aggregation happens?
questions.explanation: WHERE filters rows before grouping, while HAVING filters groups after aggregation.

questions.prompt: Without an ORDER BY clause, SQL does not guarantee the order in which a query returns its rows.
questions.explanation: Row order is only guaranteed when ORDER BY is specified, so results may come back in any order otherwise.

questions.prompt: A table employees has columns id, name, and dept. Which query returns the names of Sales employees sorted from A to Z?

options.text: SELECT name FROM employees WHERE dept = 'Sales' ORDER BY name DESC;
SELECT dept FROM employees WHERE dept = 'Sales' ORDER BY name;
SELECT name FROM employees ORDER BY name WHERE dept = 'Sales';
SELECT name FROM employees WHERE dept = 'Sales' ORDER BY name ASC;

questions.explanation: It selects the name column, filters with WHERE before sorting, and ASC sorts A to Z.

questions.prompt: Which SQL keyword, placed right after SELECT, removes duplicate rows from the result? Answer with one word.
questions.explanation: SELECT DISTINCT returns each unique row only once.

questions.prompt: A customers table and an orders table are linked by customer_id. Which join returns only customers that have at least one matching order?
questions.explanation: INNER JOIN keeps only rows that have a match in both tables.

questions.prompt:
Given an orders table with columns id, customer_id, and total, what does this query return?

SELECT customer_id, COUNT(*) FROM orders GROUP BY customer_id HAVING COUNT(*) > 2;

options.text: Each customer with more than 2 orders, plus their order count
Each customer with exactly 2 orders, plus their order count
Every order whose total is greater than 2, grouped by customer
The two customers who have placed the most orders overall

questions.explanation: GROUP BY counts orders per customer and HAVING keeps only the groups whose count is greater than 2.

questions.prompt: The condition salary = NULL returns the rows where salary is NULL.
questions.explanation: Comparing anything to NULL with = yields unknown rather than true, so you must use IS NULL.

questions.prompt:
Tables: students(id, name) and enrollments(student_id, course). What value does a student with no enrollments get in column n?

SELECT s.name, COUNT(e.course) AS n FROM students s LEFT JOIN enrollments e ON e.student_id = s.id GROUP BY s.id, s.name;
questions.explanation: The LEFT JOIN keeps the student with NULL course values, and COUNT(e.course) ignores NULLs, giving 0.

questions.prompt: Which of the following ignore NULL values in the price column? Select all that apply.
questions.explanation: SUM, AVG, and COUNT(column) skip NULLs, while COUNT(*) counts every row.

questions.prompt: Which keyword combines the results of two SELECT statements into one result and removes duplicate rows? Answer with one word.
questions.explanation: UNION merges the two result sets and removes duplicates, whereas UNION ALL keeps them.

questions.prompt: Which statements about database indexes are true? Select all that apply.

options.text: They can speed up lookups that filter on the indexed column
They add overhead to INSERT and UPDATE operations
They guarantee that every query will run faster
They remove the need to back up the table

questions.explanation: Indexes speed up reads on the indexed column but must be maintained on writes, and they help only some queries.

questions.prompt: A correlated subquery can reference columns from the outer query it is nested in.
questions.explanation: A correlated subquery depends on the outer query's current row and is logically evaluated for each of those rows.

questions.prompt: A table scores has rows (A, 90), (B, 85), (C, 85), (D, 70) for (name, pts). Using RANK() OVER (ORDER BY pts DESC), what rank does D receive?
questions.explanation: RANK leaves a gap after ties, so B and C both get 2 and D gets 4 (DENSE_RANK would give 3).

questions.prompt:
Table customers has ids 1, 2, 3. Table orders has customer_id values 2, 2, 3. How many rows does this query return?

SELECT c.id FROM customers c LEFT JOIN orders o ON o.customer_id = c.id;
questions.explanation: Customer 1 appears once with NULLs, customer 2 matches two orders, and customer 3 matches one, for 4 rows.

questions.prompt:
Table a has ids 1, 2, 3. Table b has a ref_id column containing the values 1 and NULL. What does this query return?

SELECT id FROM a WHERE id NOT IN (SELECT ref_id FROM b);
questions.explanation: When the NOT IN list contains NULL, the comparison is unknown for every non-matching id, so no rows qualify.
